pageCache.pageTitle: Our aims and ethos | Hatherop Castle Prep School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Hatherop Castle School provides a happy, safe environment which encourages children to be ambitious and develop character through our core Hatherop values whilst enjoying and benefiting from the Adventure of Childhood.
Hatherop’s Aims
Hatherop Castle School provides a happy, safe environment which encourages children to be ambitious and develop character through our core Hatherop values whilst enjoying and benefiting from the Adventure of Childhood.
Provide a happy, stimulating and safe environment in which children can thrive and enjoy the adventure of childhood.
A strong culture of safeguarding within our school community ensures everyone feels safe, secure and happy. Hatherop pupils enjoy the adventure of childhood, thrive on friendship, respect and tolerance in a healthy, positive and purposeful community.
Our strong pastoral system ensures all of our pupils are cared for and known and allowed to be individuals by the whole school community.
To challenge, promote and support each child to be ambitious academically, in the visual and performing arts and on the sports field.
We provide a rich, enjoyable, inspiring, broad, but balanced curriculum.
Expert and enthusiastic teachers deliver high quality, specialist teaching aimed at providing pupils with the ability make accelerated progress in all subjects.
Excellent facilities, well-resourced classrooms, and small class sizes allow children to engage, be inspired and develop a love of learning.
Hatherop’s environment ensures children develop an appreciation for the outdoors through our stunning grounds and environment which includes 2 Forest Schools.
Provide varied and interesting extra-curriculum which provides opportunities for all pupils to
Develop kind, tolerant and confident human beings who are prepared for life after Hatherop.
Provide a culture and environment of inclusivity and feeling of belonging, where a positive attitude and kindness matter and lifelong friendships are established.
Hatherop pupils will be well mannered, polite global citizens who are empathetic, thinking about others before themselves.
Encourage a culture of equality, diversity and inclusivity, where pupils have respect for other faiths, cultures and communities beyond Hatherop walls.
An individual and supported approach to finding the right school for the child after Hatherop in terms of academic requirements and the school that suits the individual.
Developing children’s character and equipping them with the values and skills to be positive citizens in the modern world.
Hatherop’s Values
Our Hatherop values have been devised and supported by our pupils and wider community to build young learners and leaders at Hatherop Castle. There are two important pillars which are at the heart of what Hatherop aims to deliver in our pupils. These are character and ambition.
Happiness: All members of our community should act and behave so we all can be happy.
Adventure: We play and learn with a sense of adventure
Teamwork: We work and play collaboratively and understand that we can excel and achieve more when we work as a team.
Honesty: We learn from making mistakes and we want all members of our community to show honesty towards each other.
Encouragement: We actively encourage everyone to strive for excellence in work and play.
Respect: Every member of the Hatherop community is treated with respect and kindness.
Opportunity: We make the most of every opportunity.
Perseverance: We do not give up when we find something hard or challenging.

pageCache.pageTitle: About us | Hatherop Castle, day and boarding prep school
pageCache.text:
Welcome to Hatherop Castle School, a day and boarding school where children from 2 to 13 years old can enjoy the Adventure of Childhood.
The glorious Cotswold setting, the outstanding education, and the broad and inspiring opportunities enjoyed by Hatherop Castle pupils, create a learning adventure all children can enjoy. Our academic results, which ensure all pupils gain their first choice of Senior School, tell their own story. But this is just one outcome of an education at Hatherop Castle, and it is the rest of the experience that makes us stand out from the crowd.
“Pupils throughout the school display consistently excellent attitudes towards school, achievement and learning.”
Our aspiration is that each child will have his or her own unique adventure within the castle and grounds. It is a magical place in which to spend a childhood, and here our children are challenged and supported to explore the world and their surroundings, try new things, take risks, grow in ability and confidence and fulfil their potential, whether that be in the classroom, on the sports fields or in art, music and drama.
They develop important learning characteristics that stand them in good stead for the years to come; resilience, perseverance, curiosity and the confidence to step outside their comfort zones. Our children celebrate their strengths and recognise the areas they need to work on, developing an enduring love of learning.
In a world where children can grow up too quickly, we have created an environment that allows children to remain children longer, exploring and enjoying their childhood, while helping them prepare for the next stage of their lives in a caring, nurturing environment where mistakes can be made and learnt from and each child is allowed to develop and mature naturally.
Exploring our website, you have taken the first step towards your child’s Adventure of Childhood at Hatherop Castle. You can read our interactive Storybook, which will give you a stronger sense of life here. We hope you are inspired to come for a visit, and to discover what makes Hatherop Castle so special. We look forward to meeting you and your children.

pageCache.pageTitle: Inspection Reports - Hatherop Castle Prep School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
We are delighted to share the findings of our latest Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspection, which confirms that Hatherop Castle School meets all Independent School Standards across every area of school life. The report recognises the strength of our leadership, the quality of teaching, the breadth of our curriculum and, above all, the outstanding care and support provided to every child. It also highlights our nurturing environment, where pupils are encouraged to achieve their full academic potential while developing confidence, kindness, resilience and a genuine love of learning.
Inspectors recognised that our vision is brought to life every day through ambitious teaching, exceptional pastoral care and a wealth of opportunities both inside and outside the classroom. They noted that leaders and staff act in the best interests of pupils, that children thrive in a broad and engaging curriculum, and that the school successfully fosters a respectful, inclusive community where pupils enjoy the adventure of childhood.
Independent schools are inspected by the Independent Schools Inspectorate on behalf of the Department for Education to ensure they meet the required standards. Below are just some of the many highlights from our latest inspection, with a link to the full report available at the end of the page.
What they said about our pupils
Our pupils thrive in a broad, balanced and engaging curriculum, making good progress as teachers adapt learning effectively to meet individual needs.
Pupils demonstrate positive attitudes to learning, showing confidence, curiosity and enthusiasm both in the classroom and beyond.
Our school community is built on kindness and respect. Pupils collaborate well, celebrate one another’s achievements and contribute positively to school life.
Pupils enjoy a wealth of opportunities beyond the classroom, developing their talents through an extensive programme of sport, creative arts, leadership and extra-curricular activities.
Pupils of all abilities, including those with SEND and those learning English as an additional language, are well supported through tailored teaching and specialist guidance, enabling them to learn effectively and flourish.
What they said about learning
Our broad, balanced and engaging curriculum combines academic, creative and technological subjects, inspiring pupils to develop a wide range of knowledge, skills and interests.
Teachers use secure subject knowledge, carefully planned lessons and engaging teaching methods to challenge pupils, build confidence and help every child make good progress.
As pupils move through the school, specialist teaching across subjects including science, computing, languages, music and the expressive arts enables them to deepen their understanding and extend their learning.
Our innovative electives programme allows older pupils to explore new interests and develop practical skills in areas such as robotics, business studies, sports psychology, countryside conservation and child development, preparing them for the future.
Learning is carefully structured so that pupils build on previous knowledge, think independently and apply their skills across a wide range of subjects, both inside and beyond the classroom.
What they say about the Early Years
Our Early Years setting is recognised as effective and well led, with a nurturing environment where every child is encouraged to develop curiosity, confidence and a love of learning.
Staff skilfully tailor activities to each child’s individual needs, promoting language, social development and ensuring children make good progress towards their learning goals.
From Nursery onwards, children develop strong early reading skills through high-quality phonics teaching and, by the end of Reception, are confident readers who can spell common words independently.
Children build secure mathematical understanding through engaging, hands-on learning, developing confidence as they identify shapes, solve problems and explore mathematical concepts.
Thoughtfully planned activities, expert teaching and a detailed understanding of every child ensure pupils are well prepared for a successful transition into Year 1.
What they say about Boarding
Our boarding environment is welcoming, comfortable and nurturing, providing pupils with a true home from home where they feel safe, happy and supported.
Dedicated boarding staff care for every child with kindness, ensuring pupils’ pastoral needs are met while encouraging independence, confidence and personal growth.
Boarders benefit from structured homework sessions supervised by teaching staff, helping them to develop effective study habits, independence and excellent time management skills.
A varied programme of evening and weekend activities enriches the boarding experience, giving pupils opportunities to try new activities, develop friendships and make the most of life at Hatherop.
Boarders are encouraged to share their views and contribute to the continual development of boarding, ensuring their experience remains positive, supportive and enjoyable.
What they say about our Staff
Our leaders and staff share a clear vision for the school, working together to ensure every child is supported to achieve their academic potential while flourishing personally.
Teachers combine secure subject knowledge with engaging, well-planned lessons that inspire curiosity, build confidence and enable every pupil to make good progress.
Staff know every child as an individual, adapting teaching and providing tailored support to ensure all pupils feel valued, challenged and encouraged to succeed.
Pastoral care is at the heart of school life. Leaders and staff work together to promote pupils’ health, safety and emotional wellbeing, creating a kind, respectful community where every child can thrive.
Our staff foster high expectations alongside warmth and encouragement, celebrating pupils’ achievements and nurturing the confidence, resilience and character that prepare them for life beyond Hatherop.

pageCache.pageTitle: Life after Hatherop Castle | Private Prep School & Nursery
pageCache.text:
Choosing the next school for your child is an important decision and one we at Hatherop take very seriously. Hatherop Castle feeds into a wide range of the region’s top senior schools.
Our carefully tailored Common Entrance programme ensures that all children leaving us at the end of year 8 go to their first choice of senior school often with scholarships and awards. While the majority of our pupils leave at 13 we do prepare and support children who leave us to join State and Grammar schools at the end of Prep 6.
Different schools suit different children depending on their strengths and personality. At Hatherop we know our pupils very well and work with parents to advise on which Senior Schools is right for their child. In 2025, we sent prep 8 pupils to the following schools: Bloxham, Marlborough College, Westonbirt School, Dean Close, Cheltenham College, Malvern College, Stowe, Roedean School, Rendcomb College, Monkton Combe School and Pikeroad High School, Alabama.

pageCache.pageTitle: Hatherop Castle Honours Its Special Operations Executive History - Hatherop Castle Prep School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
Hatherop Castle School has marked an important chapter in its history with a special Service of Commemoration and Thanksgiving, honouring the personnel of Special Training School 45 (STS 45), the Special Operations Executive (SOE) and other Allied Services who trained and served at Hatherop Castle during the Second World War.
The school was privileged to welcome dignitaries and serving military personnel, alongside pupils, staff and members of the wider community, for the commemorative service at St Nicholas Church. The congregation then returned to Hatherop Castle for the unveiling and dedication of a permanent memorial plaque.
During the Second World War, Hatherop Castle became home to STS 45 and played its part in the work of the Special Operations Executive. The service provided an opportunity not only to commemorate those connected with this remarkable period in the Castle’s history, but also to ensure their stories continue to be understood by future generations.
For today’s Hatherop pupils, the occasion offered a powerful connection between history and the place in which they learn every day. The buildings and grounds around them are more than the setting for their education; they are part of a much wider story.
Understanding this heritage helps bring history beyond the classroom, encouraging pupils to consider the experiences of those who came before them and the importance of remembrance, service and responsibility. The permanent memorial will now provide a lasting reminder of the men and women connected with Hatherop Castle during the war.
Hatherop Castle School is proud to play its part in preserving this important history and ensuring that the courage, service and sacrifice of those who trained and served here are remembered with gratitude and honour for generations to come.

pageCache.pageTitle: Number Confidence Week: Getting Hatherop Talking About Maths! - Hatherop Castle Prep School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
How many trees are there at Hatherop Castle? How many steps would it take to walk around the school grounds? And how can a simple question spark a whole school conversation about Maths?
This week, Hatherop Castle School is celebrating Number Confidence Week, with a series of fun, thought-provoking activities designed to get pupils, teachers and families talking about numbers, sharing ideas and discovering that Maths is about much more than finding the right answer.
Led by our Head of Maths, Mr Hammond, the week aims to build confidence, encourage curiosity and show children that mathematical thinking is something we use every day, often without even realising it.
No Wrong Answers, Just Brilliant Thinking!
Each morning, pupils across the school will begin their day with a special mathematical challenge during registration. From Reception through to Prep 8, every class will tackle exactly the same estimation question, but the conversations and approaches will look wonderfully different.
Our youngest pupils might use drawings, objects or imaginative demonstrations to explain their thinking, while older pupils will explore calculations, make assumptions and consider margins of error.
The emphasis isn’t on getting the answer right. In fact, there won’t even be an answer sheet!
Instead, children will be encouraged to make an initial guess, discuss their reasoning, listen to different perspectives and perhaps even change their minds along the way.
As Mr Hammond explains, the aim is to encourage mathematical conversations, where even the wildest guesses can lead to some of the most interesting discussions.
By removing the pressure of finding one correct answer, pupils can develop the confidence to explore ideas, ask questions and explain their thinking without worrying about making mistakes.
A Mathematical Treasure Hunt!
The mathematical adventures won’t stop in the classroom!
Throughout the week, children will also have the opportunity to take part in a Maths Treasure Hunt around the school, encouraging them to put their problem-solving skills to the test as they explore their surroundings.
It’s a chance to discover that Maths isn’t confined to textbooks and classrooms. Numbers, patterns, measurements and mathematical challenges can be found all around us.
Bringing Maths Home
We’re also inviting our families to join in the fun!
Every day this week, we’ll be sharing a Family Maths Challenge on our social media stories, giving parents and children a chance to tackle a question together.
Whether it’s a conversation around the dinner table, a little friendly competition between siblings or a family debate about the most sensible estimate, we hope these challenges will inspire plenty of mathematical conversations at home.
There’s no need for complicated calculations or specialist knowledge. Just a little curiosity, some creative thinking and a willingness to have a go!
Tune In to Our Latest Hatherop Podcast!
To coincide with Number Confidence Week, we’ve also released the latest episode of our Hatherop podcast, Episode 7: Maths at Hatherop, featuring our very own Mr Hammond.
In this episode, we explore the importance of developing mathematical confidence, how we approach Maths at Hatherop and why encouraging children to talk about numbers can make such a difference to their learning.
It’s a wonderful opportunity for parents to gain an insight into the thinking behind our Maths teaching and discover how mathematical curiosity can be encouraged beyond the classroom.
🎧 Listen to Episode 7: Maths at Hatherop – Numeracy Confidence Week | Listen to the Podcast on Spotify
Building Confidence, One Conversation at a Time
At Hatherop, we believe that developing confidence in Maths is just as important as developing mathematical skills.
Being willing to have a go, explain an idea, question an assumption or learn from someone else’s approach are all valuable skills that extend far beyond the Maths classroom.
Number Confidence Week is a celebration of exactly that: curiosity, collaboration, problem-solving and the confidence to think differently.
So, whether you’re estimating, calculating, debating or simply making your best guess, we hope everyone in the Hatherop community will get involved this week. After all, every great mathematical discovery starts with a question!

pageCache.pageTitle: A Happy Start to the Year in Nursery - Hatherop Castle Prep School and Nursery
pageCache.text:
September has brought happy faces, new friendships and plenty of adventures as we welcomed our children back after the summer, alongside some lovely new faces joining our Nursery family. We have been incredibly proud of how happily and confidently everyone has settled into the new term.
Our All About Me topic has been the perfect way to begin the year, giving the children opportunities to get to know one another, celebrate what makes each of us unique and discover all the things we have in common.
In Pre-Reception, this has even extended into our mathematical thinking, as the children searched for friends who “matched” them. Of course, one particularly important question needed answering: “Do you have flashing shoes?”
Our morning Name Game has also become an important part of the daily routine. Each child finds their own name and places it into our special jar when they arrive, helping to develop independence, name recognition and those all-important early literacy skills.
Creativity has been flowing too. Our budding artists have created wonderfully individual self-portraits, beginning with a photograph of their face before painting and decorating the rest of themselves. Colourful clothes, hats, glasses and even the occasional moustache have made each portrait completely unique!
Our new family photo books have proved another lovely addition to Nursery life. Filled with photographs of special people and much-loved pets, they have sparked wonderful conversations and provided a comforting connection between home and school.
There has been plenty of activity beyond the classroom too. Mr Bailey has introduced the children to rugby, with our Toddlers becoming familiar with rugby balls, although not always in the traditional way, while Pre-Reception have been developing their throwing skills and learning how to score tries.
Music has filled Nursery with the return of Boogie Babies, as Miss Scott leads the children through songs, dancing and movement. Mrs Vaughn has also introduced rhythm sticks, encouraging the children to listen carefully and explore different sounds, beats and actions.
Meanwhile, Pre-Reception have taken their first steps into French with Madame Christie and her bears, Annic A, enjoying the excitement of discovering a new language together.
We even made the most of the September sunshine with a trip to the village park, where the children enjoyed exploring, playing and spending time together in our local community.
It has been wonderful to watch the children embrace Nursery life, exploring their classrooms, reconnecting with familiar friends, making new ones and enthusiastically getting involved in everything on offer.
There have been songs sung, portraits painted, rugby balls thrown, French words spoken, families shared, park adventures enjoyed and, importantly, flashing shoes compared.
It has been a busy, joyful and adventure-filled start to the year, and we cannot wait to see what October brings.
